title: Report it in the first minute
brief: 18:28. A file share notification lands in every finance inbox at once. The clock starts now.
insight: The same phishing email usually goes to everyone. The first report is what lets IT pull it before the next person clicks.
teaches: Report the moment something looks wrong: the first minute matters most
Report even if you clicked. Especially if you clicked
Use the button in Mail, or ring the service desk; do not just delete it

mail.subject: Marta Okafor shared “Bonus letters 2026.pdf” with you
body: Marta Okafor shared a file with you on Filebridge.

body.small: You received this because you are a member of Veltrix Logistics on Filebridge.

headers.summary: A lookalike of filebridge.io, sent to the whole finance team at the same moment.

choices.label: A fake Filebridge share just went to the finance team

script.say: Thank you, that is exactly what I need. I am pulling it from every inbox now. If you clicked, tell me, no blame. Log it with Report phishing too.

setup.title: Mail
setup.body: Marta Okafor shared “Bonus letters 2026.pdf” with you

outcome.label: Reported it inside the first minute
outcome.what: Your report was the first. IT pulled the email before anyone else clicked.
outcome.ideal: reports the moment something looks wrong.

outcome.label: Reported it, a little late
outcome.what: Reported, but not before a colleague had already signed in on the fake page.
outcome.ideal: reports in the first minute, before anyone else clicks.

outcome.label: Rang the service desk as well
outcome.what: A call gets a human moving straight away.
outcome.ideal: rings the service desk when something is spreading.

decide.objective: A suspicious share has reached the whole team. Act fast.
decide.insight: Deleting it protects you. Reporting it protects everyone who has not opened it yet.

hint.text: Open the email, check the sender's real address, and press Report phishing. Then ring the service desk on 4040.

message.text: anyone else get a bonus letter from Marta? signed in to read it and it just went blank
Marta is on leave, she has not shared anything. Do not open it!

outcome.label: Signed in on the fake share
outcome.what: Your password went to the attacker. What matters most now is how fast you say so.
outcome.ideal: reports straight away, even after clicking.

card.title: Now the clock matters even more
body: The page was {{fb.host}}, not filebridge.io. It happens, to careful people too.
What decides how bad this gets is the next minute: report it and tell the service desk you signed in, so they can reset your password and pull the email from everyone else.
card.ideal: reports at once, including their own click.

outcome.label: Reported the fake share
outcome.what: The service desk pulled it from 23 inboxes.

message.text: Heads up: that Filebridge share was fake, not from Marta. Priya has pulled it from everyone's inbox. Thanks Sam for the quick report.

card.title: An early warning for everyone
body: One report, and the service desk pulled the email from every inbox on the floor. The people who had not opened it yet never will.
The fastest security control you have is the Report button. Use it the moment something looks wrong, and ring the desk when it is spreading.

own-up.objective: Report it now, and say that you signed in.

hint.text: Press Report phishing in Mail, and ring the service desk on 4040 (or raise a ticket) to say you signed in.

outcome.label: Reported it, including your own click
outcome.what: Your password is reset and the email is pulled from everyone else's inbox.
outcome.ideal: owns up fast; no blame, just speed.
